text:
These days, I believe polyamory is often a way to cope with an inability to connect deeply with one person, or a way to admit a lack of self-control without necessarily doing the self-development that would make the arrangement ethical.

That doesn't describe everyone doing polyamory. If you know you can't do monogamy, I'd rather you say so than promise it.

The stranger situation is when both people know something is changing and neither one says it. Maybe one is attracted to somebody else. Maybe the feelings in the relationship are changing. Sometimes possessiveness gets called love on top of it. The concealment can end up doing more damage than the outside connection would have.

Love is real. The form built around it can still be broken. A foundational, permanent, exclusive romantic partnership is promised far more often than it is actually lived.
